toc.title: Reading, answering, shortcuts and staying calm

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Pace the 65 questions in 90 minutes with checkpoints
  • Use a four-step method: read, predict, eliminate, confirm
  • Handle multiple-response, ordering and matching questions, qualifier words and look-alike traps
  • Plan your final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake

2Reading, answering, shortcuts and staying calm

Running case

Cedar and Salt's Mock Exam

  • A teammate sat a practice exam and finished just under the pass mark
  • The review showed lost points, not lost knowledge: misread questions, look-alike services and blank answers
  • The course content is covered; now technique has to match it
  • Your job: turn what you know into points

The Exam Clock Beyond the guide

  • 65 questions in 90 minutes is about 83 seconds each
  • Aim for about 70 seconds on a first pass; the spare time is for the hard questions
  • Use checkpoints as the latest you should reach: question 20 by minute 28, 40 by 55, 65 by 85
  • 15 questions are unscored and you cannot tell which, so treat every one as real

Exam tip: If you are behind at a checkpoint, answer quickly and move on; a blank always scores zero.

Read for the Requirement Beyond the guide

  • Read the last line first: it holds what is being asked (a tip from AWS's own certification blog)
  • Then read the scenario and underline the requirement words: most cost-effective, least operational overhead, most secure, quickest to build
  • Note the verb: filter, detect, explain, ground, evaluate, audit, encrypt
  • Note the subject: the model, the data, the prompt, the agent or the account
  • Predict the answer before you look at the options

Exam tip: The scenario is the story; the last line is the test.

A Four-Step Answer Method Beyond the guide

  • Read: the last line first, then the scenario
  • Predict: name the service or idea before you see the options
  • Eliminate: remove the options that are clearly wrong
  • Confirm: match the requirement word and the verb to what is left

Exam tip: A prediction stops a plausible distractor from pulling you off course.

Eliminating Distractors Beyond the guide

  • Distractors are real services and ideas that sound plausible, so ask why each one fails
  • Wrong job: it does something else (Guardrails filters; Clarify finds bias)
  • Wrong effort: fine-tuning or pre-training when a prompt or RAG would do
  • Wrong tool: SageMaker AI when Bedrock needs less effort, or the reverse
  • Half true: one clause fits and another does not
  • Words such as always and never deserve a second look

Exam tip: Remove two of four options and a guess is right half the time.

Multiple-Response Questions Beyond the guide

  • A multiple-response question has two or more correct answers among five or more options
  • The question tells you how many to choose, such as Select TWO
  • The guide says you must select all correct responses to receive credit
  • Judge each option on its own, true or false against the question, then count
  • Choose exactly the number asked

Exam tip: If three options fit, reread the question for the word that rules one out.

Ordering and Matching Questions Beyond the guide

Type What the guide says How to approach it
Ordering A list of three to five responses to complete a task; select and place them in order Find the first and last steps, then fill the middle
Matching A list of responses to match with three to seven prompts; match all pairs correctly Start with the pairs you are sure of; the rest get easier
  • Both are all or nothing per the guide, so check every position before you move on

Exam tip: Know the order of the lifecycles and the one-line job of each service.

Qualifier Words Steer the Answer Beyond the guide

If the question says… Think…
Most cost-effective A smaller model, prompt engineering or RAG before tuning; batch for jobs that can wait; on-demand for spiky use
Least operational overhead Managed: Bedrock, Knowledge Bases, Guardrails
Most control SageMaker AI and your own models
Current or private data RAG with a knowledge base
Consistent answers A low temperature
Least privilege, most secure IAM roles, KMS, PrivateLink, narrow permissions
Explain or document Explainable model, Model Cards, source citation

Exam tip: Underline the qualifier: it is the word that picks one correct answer from several that work.

Generative AI Question Shortcuts

The symptom Think…
Invented facts RAG grounding, contextual grounding check
Different answers to the same prompt Nondeterminism: lower the temperature
Harmful content, personal data Guardrails filters
Task skill from labeled examples Fine-tuning
Jargon from unlabeled text Domain adaptation, continued pre-training
Big model too costly Distillation, or a smaller model
Repeated long context Prompt caching
Who did it, what changed CloudTrail; Config

Exam tip: Most questions are pattern matching: name the symptom first, then the fix.

When You Are Unsure Beyond the guide

  • Never leave a question blank: the guide says an unanswered question counts as incorrect and a guess has no penalty
  • Eliminate first, then choose between what is left
  • When two answers fit, prefer the one that is managed, least privilege and simplest
  • This is a foundational exam: answers that need coding, tuning or building pipelines are less likely
  • Change an answer only when you find a specific reason
  • If the screen lets you mark a question to revisit, use it for hard ones, and check the exam tutorial

Exam tip: A blank always scores zero; a guess might not.

3Preparation and practice

Your Final Week Beyond the guide

When Do this
Seven days out Read the current exam guide again and check for changes
Six to four days out Redo the questions for your two weakest domains; write your own look-alike notes
Three days out Take a timed run of about 65 questions in 90 minutes; AWS offers free practice question sets
Two days out Read module 15 once, then say the lists aloud
The day before A light review, a good night's sleep and your exam-day logistics

Exam tip: Practice under the clock: pace is a skill, and it improves with repetition.

Exam Day and Afterwards [Verify live]

  • Delivery: at a Pearson VUE test center or online with a proctor; read the provider's rules
  • Fee: USD 100; a pass is valid for 3 years
  • Results: posted to your AWS Certification Account within five business days after the exam, unless held for review
  • If you do not pass: wait 14 calendar days; there is no limit on attempts and each one needs the full fee
  • If you pass: you cannot retake the same exam for two years
  • As of 5 November 2026: AWS may change fees and policies, so read its pages before you book

Exam tip: Policies and fees change; check AWS's certification pages before you book.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Mock Exam

What went wrong Technique to apply
Ran short of time in the last ten questions Checkpoints: question 20 by minute 28, 40 by minute 55
Chose fine-tuning for "quickest and cheapest" Read the qualifier: prompts or RAG come first
Picked one answer in a "Select TWO" question Judge each option and choose exactly two
Put lifecycle steps in the wrong order Anchor the first and last steps, then fill the middle
Left three questions blank Answer every one: there is no penalty
Chose Clarify to filter harmful output Read the verb: filtering is Guardrails
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Cedar and Salt wants a chatbot to answer from policy documents that change every week, with the least operational overhead. Which solution fits best?

  • APre-train a new foundation model each time the policies change
  • BAmazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which provides managed RAG
  • CFine-tune a model every week with the new policy text
  • DSelf-host an open model and write all the retrieval code
Show the answer

Answer: B. The requirement words are current documents and least operational overhead. Knowledge Bases is managed RAG, so updating the data source is enough. Pre-training and fine-tuning cost time and money every week, and self-hosting adds operations.

S2Cedar and Salt wants to keep Amazon Bedrock traffic private and limit who can call a model. Which TWO actions help? (Select TWO.)

  • ACreate an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Bedrock
  • BShare one long-term access key across all teams
  • CGive applications IAM roles with least-privilege policies
  • DAllow every principal to perform every action on the endpoint
  • ETurn off logging so that fewer people see the activity
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. PrivateLink keeps traffic off the internet, and IAM roles with narrow policies limit who can call a model. Shared keys, open endpoint policies and disabled logging weaken security.

S3Cedar and Salt's assistant performs well overall but poorly for guests who write in one language. What is the best first step?

  • AIncrease the temperature so that replies become more varied for everyone
  • BSwitch to the largest model available without testing it on that language
  • CCache the prompts used by the application to reduce the response time
  • DCompare the results by language group, which is subgroup analysis
Show the answer

Answer: D. Unequal results across groups point to bias, and subgroup analysis shows where the gap is. Then improve the data, add representative examples and monitor. Temperature, model size and caching do not address the cause.

S4With six minutes left, a candidate has four questions unanswered and is unsure of each. Based on the exam guide's scoring rules, what should they do?

  • AAnswer all four, since a blank scores zero and a guess has no penalty
  • BLeave all four blank, because wrong answers will lower the whole score
  • CAnswer only the two that feel most likely, and leave the other two blank
  • DSpend the remaining time rechecking earlier answers instead of guessing
Show the answer

Answer: A. The exam guide says unanswered questions are scored as incorrect and there is no penalty for guessing. A guess can only help; a blank always scores zero.

S5Auditors ask Cedar and Salt for AWS's compliance reports and for the history of changes to its resource configurations. Which TWO services fit? (Select TWO.)

  • AAWS Artifact, for AWS's compliance reports
  • BAmazon Macie, for finding sensitive data in S3
  • CAWS Config, for configuration history and rules
  • DAmazon Polly, for turning text into speech
  • EAmazon Inspector, for finding exposed passwords in prompts
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Artifact provides on-demand compliance reports, and Config records resource configuration and its history. Macie finds sensitive data, Polly is text to speech, and Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pace 65 questions, 90 minutes, about 83 seconds each, with checkpoints
Method read the last line, predict, eliminate, confirm
Types multiple choice, multiple response, ordering and matching, with all-or-nothing credit on the last three
Traps look-alike services, qualifier words and absolute words
Unsure never leave a blank; there is no penalty for guessing
Plan a final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake after 14 days
